articles.title: Employer Health Benefit Costs Projected to Top $20K Per Employee by 2027
articles.summary: Employer-sponsored health benefit costs are projected to surpass $20,000 per employee by 2027, driven largely by escalating specialty drug and pharmacy spend. This rising cost trajectory increases pressure on self-funded employers to adopt aggressive PBM strategies, transparent pricing models, and specialized cost-management tools.

articles.title: Bipartisan Policy Center Highlights State-Level PBM Reform Trends
articles.summary: The Bipartisan Policy Center has released a case study examining recent state-level legislative efforts to reform pharmacy benefit managers. This analysis provides self-funded employers and PBMs with insight into emerging regulatory trends, such as transparency mandates and spread pricing bans. Understanding these state policy shifts is crucial for employers navigating multi-state plan compliance and cost management strategies.
articles.source_line: Source: Bipartisan Policy Center; Tue, 24 Nov 2026

articles.title: Florida Attorney General Fights to Keep PBM Price-Fixing Lawsuit in State Court
articles.summary: Florida's AG is pushing to keep a state-level antitrust and price-fixing lawsuit against major pharmacy benefit managers in state court rather than federal jurisdiction. This ongoing litigation reflects the broader wave of state-level regulatory and legal scrutiny targeting PBM pricing and business practices, which directly impacts self-funded employer health plans monitoring market reform.

articles.title: The Urgency of Enforcing PBM Reform and Regulatory Compliance
articles.summary: This article examines the critical need for enforcement mechanisms surrounding recent pharmacy benefit manager (PBM) reforms. For self-funded employers and transparent PBMs, strict oversight of PBM practices is vital to ensuring promised cost savings and transparency are actually realized.
articles.source_line: Source: Drug Topics; Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:07:23 GMT

articles.title: Congressman DeSaulnier Introduces Legislation to Prohibit PBM Kickbacks
articles.summary: Representative Mark DeSaulnier has introduced a new bill aimed at prohibiting health plan and PBM kickbacks to protect consumers from rising costs. This legislative push directly impacts PBM pricing models, transparency, and rebate practices that affect self-funded employer health plans.
articles.source_line: Source: Congressman Mark Desaulnier (.gov); Tue, 24 Nov 2026 21:26:26 GMT

articles.title: Open Enrollment Highlights Rising Benefit Costs for Employers
articles.summary: Rising healthcare and pharmacy benefit costs are placing significant financial pressure on employers during open enrollment, pushing budgets toward critical thresholds. This trend directly impacts self-funded plans seeking sustainable cost-management strategies and alternative pricing models to control escalating medical and pharmaceutical spend.
articles.source_line: Source: Insurance Business; Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:23:17 GMT

articles.title: JPMorgan Wins ERISA Lawsuit Over Prescription Drug Costs
articles.summary: A federal court ruled in favor of JPMorgan Chase in an ERISA class action alleging the company mismanagement of its employee health plan's pharmacy benefits. The decision provides a critical legal benchmark for self-funded employers navigating fiduciary duties regarding PBM contract pricing and drug spend. The outcome underscores the ongoing legal exposure employers face regarding plan costs, even as plan sponsors successfully defend their benefit administration.
